label: Left realm flag tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the realm flag of the left side in the battle summary window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of a widget in the battle summary window. It returns text.

label: Left side result
summary: The result data of the left side of the battle (a combat side result).
details: Vanilla reads the side's commander, its loss percentage and its initial number of soldiers from it. The result is an object, so more functions are chained on it.

label: Left soldier stats
summary: Going by its name, a list of soldier statistics for the left side, used to fill a list in the battle summary window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model (the list a widget repeats its rows over) in the window. What exactly each row holds is not documented; the game lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Left total tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the total of the left side in the battle summary window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of a widget in the window. It returns text.

label: Battle location
summary: Going by its name, the place where the battle was fought.
details: Vanilla reads the terrain from it for a terrain display, and the battle title text names it. The result is an object, so more functions are chained on it.

label: Battle name
summary: Text, most likely the name of the battle shown in the battle summary window.
details: Nothing in the input uses this function on the battle summary window; this rests on its name and its text return type.

label: Knight outcome text
summary: Going by its name, text about the outcome for the given character in the battle.
details: Vanilla puts it right after a knight's prowess in the knight's line of the summary, passing the knight itself. The exact wording it returns is not shown in the input.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose outcome is described.

label: Opponent side result
summary: The result data of the battle side opposing the player (a combat side result).
details: Nothing in the input uses it; this rests on its name and its return type, the same type as the left and right side results.

label: Player side result
summary: The result data of the battle side the player was on (a combat side result).
details: Nothing in the input uses it; this rests on its name and its return type, the same type as the left and right side results.

label: Right army stretch
summary: A whole number used as the horizontal layout stretch factor of the right army in the window, going by the name.
details: Vanilla feeds it to a horizontal layout stretch factor of a widget.

label: Right side counter list
summary: A list tied to the given men-at-arms type on the right side, used to fill a list in the battle summary window.
details: Vanilla passes the men-at-arms type itself and uses the result as a data model. Going by its name it holds what counters that type; the input does not say more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The men-at-arms type the list is built for.
fields.values: a men-at-arms type, for example MenAtArmsType.Self

label: Right side countered by list
summary: A list tied to the given men-at-arms type on the right side, used to fill a list in the battle summary window.
details: Vanilla passes the men-at-arms type itself and uses the result as a data model. Going by its name it holds what that type is countered by; the input does not say more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The men-at-arms type the list is built for.
fields.values: a men-at-arms type, for example MenAtArmsType.Self

label: Right knight stats
summary: A list of statistics rows for the knights of the right side.
details: Vanilla fills a list in the window with it and counts its entries (GetDataModelSize) for the knights header and for the enemy knights text.

label: Right side commander
summary: Most likely the commander of the right side, as a character.
details: Nothing in the input uses it on the battle summary window. The combat window has a function of the same name used as a data context, which hints at the same meaning.

label: Right commander tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the commander of the right side.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of a widget in the window. It returns text.

label: Right side main character
summary: The main character of the right side of the battle.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of widgets, reads its culture's unit look from it, and names it in the enemy knights text. More character functions can be chained on it.

label: Right realm flag tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the realm flag of the right side in the battle summary window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of a widget in the window. It returns text.

label: Right side result
summary: The result data of the right side of the battle (a combat side result).
details: Vanilla reads the side's commander, its loss percentage and its number of surviving soldiers from it. The result is an object, so more functions are chained on it.

label: Right soldier stats
summary: A list of soldier statistics for the right side, used to fill a list in the battle summary window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model (the list a widget repeats its rows over). What exactly each row holds is not documented; the game lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Right total tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the total of the right side in the battle summary window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of a widget in the window. It returns text.

label: Soldier sort selection
summary: A pair of whole numbers that says which sort entry is selected for the soldiers list.
details: Vanilla feeds it to the selected index of a sort control. What the two numbers stand for is not shown in the input.

label: Soldier sort options
summary: The list of ways the soldiers list can be sorted.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a sort control. Going by its name it holds the sort choices; the input does not say more.

label: Terrain bonus
summary: Going by its name, the terrain bonus of the given men-at-arms type in this battle, as a number.
details: Vanilla compares it with 0 to show one element when it is positive and another when it is negative.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The men-at-arms type the bonus is for.
fields.values: a men-at-arms type, for example MenAtArmsType.Self

label: War score
summary: Going by its name, the war score tied to this battle, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a percentage with a sign. The input does not say more.

label: Won or lost label
summary: The text label saying whether the battle was won or lost.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of a label in the window.

label: Go to province
summary: Does something when clicked: most likely moves the map view to the battle's province.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler. It returns nothing. Where it goes is taken from its name only.

label: Has event sequence
summary: Whether the given character has an event sequence in the battle summary.
details: Vanilla passes the right-side character and shows a tooltip only when the answer is yes. The meaning of event sequence is taken from the name.

label: Has player
summary: Whether the player took part in the battle, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it; this rests on its name and its yes/no return type.

label: Player lost
summary: Whether the player lost the battle, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it; this rests on its name and its yes/no return type.

label: Player won
summary: Whether the player won the battle, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it; this rests on its name and its yes/no return type.

label: Is auto expand
summary: Whether the auto expand option is switched on.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of a control. ToggleAutoExpand is probably what flips it.

label: Is big losses
summary: Whether the battle had big losses, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it; this rests on its name and its yes/no return type. What counts as big is not stated.

label: Is knight killed
summary: Whether the given knight was killed in the battle.
details: Vanilla passes the left-side or right-side character and shows a widget only when the answer is yes.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character, for example BattleEvent.GetLeftCharacter( BattleSummaryWindow.IsPlayerAttacker )

label: Is knight wounded
summary: Whether the given knight was wounded in the battle.
details: Vanilla passes the knight itself and shows a widget only when the answer is yes.

label: Is knights tab shown
summary: Whether the knights view of the window is the one currently shown.
details: Vanilla uses it for the pressed look of a button, to mark a widget as always transparent and to show or hide parts of the window. OnShowKnights is probably what switches to this view.

label: Is minor battle
summary: Whether the battle counts as a minor one.
details: The battle title text (BATTLE_SUMMARY_BATTLE_TITLE) uses it to choose an extra phrase for a minor battle.

label: Is player attacker
summary: Whether the player was the attacker in the battle.
details: Vanilla passes it to BattleEvent.GetLeftCharacter and GetRightCharacter to pick which character belongs on which side.

label: Is soldiers tab shown
summary: Whether the soldiers view of the window is the one currently shown.
details: Vanilla uses it for the pressed look of a button, to mark a widget as always transparent and to show or hide parts of the window. OnShowSoldiers is probably what switches to this view.

label: Is sort descending
summary: Whether the list is sorted from high to low, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it; ToggleSortOrder is probably what flips it. This rests on the names and the yes/no return type.

label: Show knights
summary: Switches the window to its knights view when clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler. It returns nothing. IsKnightsShown is probably the matching check.

label: Show soldiers
summary: Switches the window to its soldiers view when clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click handlers of two widgets. It returns nothing. IsSoldiersShown is probably the matching check.

label: Pan to left title province
summary: Most likely moves the map view to the province of the left side's title.
details: Nothing in the input uses it; this rests on its name and the fact that it returns nothing.

label: Pan to right title province
summary: Most likely moves the map view to the province of the right side's title.
details: Nothing in the input uses it; this rests on its name and the fact that it returns nothing.

label: Restore sort
summary: Applies the saved sort setting again when clicked, going by the name.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click handlers of several widgets. It returns nothing. Exactly what it restores is not shown in the input.

label: Window itself
summary: The battle summary window itself, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it on this type. Other types' Self functions are used to pass the object on to another function.

label: Set displayed phase
summary: Chooses which phase of the battle the window shows.
details: Vanilla calls it from clicks with the numbers 1, 2 and 3. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a whole number; vanilla uses 1, 2 and 3, written '(int32)1'

label: Sort knights
summary: Re-sorts the knights list when the sort selection changes.
details: Vanilla runs it from a selection-changed handler. It returns nothing.

label: Sort soldiers
summary: Re-sorts the soldiers list when the sort selection changes.
details: Vanilla runs it from a selection-changed handler. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle auto expand
summary: Switches the auto expand option on or off when clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler. It returns nothing. IsAutoExpand is probably the matching check.

label: Toggle sort order
summary: Flips the sort order between ascending and descending when clicked, going by the name.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click handlers of two widgets. It returns nothing.

label: Window access
summary: Gives access to the blackmail window object itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Nothing uses it on this type. The same function name on other window types is used to hand the object on to another function.

label: Can send offer
summary: Whether the blackmail offer can be sent now, going by the name.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of a widget in the window, so that widget is disabled when the answer is no.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the blackmail window when clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler. It returns nothing.

label: Confirmation window
summary: Going by its name, the confirmation part of the interaction, used as the data context of a widget in the blackmail window.
details: The game lists its return type as unregistered, so nothing more is documented.

label: Description
summary: The description text shown in the blackmail window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of a label in the window.

label: Secret items
summary: Going by its name, the list of secrets that can be picked in the blackmail window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the window. The BlackmailSecretItem functions are used on its rows, so each row is probably such an item.

label: Send offer tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the tooltip text for sending the offer.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of a widget in the window. It returns text.

label: Has secrets
summary: Whether there are any secrets to pick from, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it; this rests on its name and its yes/no return type.

label: Is blackmail
summary: Whether the window is in blackmail mode, going by the name.
details: Vanilla uses it to show parts of the window, together with the weak and strong hook checks of a secret item.

label: Window itself
summary: The blackmail window itself, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it on this type. Other types' Self functions are used to pass the object on to another function.

label: Send offer
summary: Sends the blackmail offer when clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler. It returns nothing.

label: Item access
summary: Gives access to the secret item object itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Nothing uses it on this type. The same function name on other types is used to hand the object on to another function.

label: Secret
summary: The secret this row stands for.
details: Vanilla reads the secret's name and its type's icon from it. The result is an object, so more functions are chained on it.

label: Item tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for this secret row.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of the row. It returns text.

label: Is enabled
summary: Whether this secret row can be used.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of the row.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this secret is the one picked.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed look of the row.

label: Is strong hook
summary: Whether this secret would give a strong hook, going by the name.
details: Vanilla shows a widget only when the window is in blackmail mode and the answer is yes. The hook strength meaning comes from the name.

label: Is weak hook
summary: Whether this secret would give only a weak hook, going by the name.
details: Vanilla shows a widget only when the window is in blackmail mode and the answer is yes. The hook strength meaning comes from the name.

label: Click item
summary: Runs the row's click action: picks or unpicks this secret.
details: Vanilla runs it from the row's click handler. It returns nothing. What it does exactly is taken from the name and IsSelected.

label: Item itself
summary: The secret item itself, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it on this type. Other types' Self functions are used to pass the object on to another function.

label: Blur access
summary: Gives access to the blur threshold setting object itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: It is part of the game's internal interface code. Nothing uses it on this type.

label: Blur threshold
summary: The current blur threshold of a map editor brush, as a decimal number.
details: Part of the engine's map editor. Vanilla uses it as the value of a slider that runs from 2 to 20 in steps of 2, and shows it in the edit box beside the slider. What the threshold blurs is not described.

label: Blur itself
summary: The blur threshold setting itself, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it on this type.

label: Set blur threshold
summary: Takes in a new blur threshold when its slider in the map editor is moved.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the blur threshold slider of the engine's map editor when the value changes; the slider passes the value itself.

label: Set blur threshold (typed)
summary: Takes in a blur threshold typed into its edit box in the map editor.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when editing of the edit box beside the blur threshold slider is finished; the edit box hands over its text.

label: Bookmark access
summary: Gives access to the bookmark object itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Nothing uses it on this type. The same function name on other types is used to hand the object on to another function.

label: Bookmark background
summary: The background picture of the bookmark, going by the name.
details: Nothing uses it directly on this type. The bookmark screen reads a function of the same name from the selected bookmark as a texture, which hints at the same meaning.

label: Button icon
summary: The button icon picture of the bookmark, going by the name.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the bookmark selection screen. The game lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Big button icon
summary: The big button icon picture of the bookmark, going by the name.
details: Nothing uses it directly on this type. The bookmark screen reads a function of the same name from the selected bookmark as a texture, which hints at the same meaning.

label: Bookmark date
summary: The date of the bookmark.
details: Vanilla reads its year from it for a text in the bookmark screen. The result is a date, so more date functions are chained on it.

label: Bookmark name
summary: The name of the bookmark, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as a label text in the bookmark selection screen.

label: Start button picture
summary: A picture for the bookmark's start button, going by the name.
details: Nothing uses it directly on this type. The bookmark screen reads a function of the same name from the selected bookmark as a texture, which hints at the same meaning.

label: Has button icon
summary: Whether the bookmark has a button icon, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it.

label: Has big button icon
summary: Whether the bookmark has a big button icon, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it.

label: Has required DLC
summary: Whether the bookmark's required DLC is available, going by the name.
details: Vanilla uses it to show parts of the bookmark screen only when the answer is yes.

label: Has start button
summary: Whether the bookmark has a start button picture, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it.

label: Is recommended
summary: Whether the bookmark is marked as recommended.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a widget in the bookmark screen only when the answer is yes.

label: Bookmark itself
summary: The bookmark itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to GameSetup.SetSelectedBookmark and GameSetup.IsBookmarkSelected to select a bookmark or ask whether it is the selected one.

label: Character access
summary: Gives access to the bookmark character object itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Nothing uses it on this type. The same function name on other types is used to hand the object on to another function.

label: Age
summary: The age of the bookmark character, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the bookmark texts, for example after the label Age.

label: Animated portrait
summary: The animated portrait picture of the bookmark character.
details: Vanilla uses it as the portrait texture in the bookmark screen. The game lists its return type as unregistered.

fields.text: The portrait environment to render in.

fields.text: The camera that frames the portrait.

label: Bookmark of the character
summary: The bookmark this character belongs to.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a widget in the bookmark screen. The game lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Culture name
summary: The name of the character's culture, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it after the label for culture in the bookmark texts.

label: Description
summary: The description text of the bookmark character.
details: Vanilla uses it as label text in the bookmark screen and in the main front-end view.

label: Difficulty
summary: The difficulty of this bookmark character, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it after the label Difficulty in the bookmark texts and screen.

label: House template
summary: The house of the bookmark character, as a house template object.
details: Vanilla reads the house's name, motto and coat of arms from it. The result is an object, so more functions are chained on it.

label: Dynasty splendor frame
summary: A whole number used as an image frame in the coat of arms interface, going by the name tied to the dynasty's splendor.
details: Vanilla uses it as the frame of an image in the shared coat of arms interface.

label: Dynasty template
summary: The dynasty of the bookmark character, as a dynasty template object.
details: Vanilla reads the dynasty's name, motto and coat of arms from it. The result is an object, so more functions are chained on it.

label: Government type
summary: The government type of the bookmark character.
details: Vanilla shows its name with its icon in the bookmark texts. The result is an object, so more functions are chained on it.

label: Screen position
summary: The position of the character on the bookmark screen, as two decimal numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the position of a widget.

label: Title template
summary: The title of the bookmark character, as a title template object.
details: Vanilla reads the title's coat of arms from it, in the bookmark screen and in the shared coat of arms interface. Which of the character's titles it is, is not shown in the input.

label: Location image
summary: A picture of the character's location, going by the name.
details: Nothing uses it directly on this type. The bookmark screen reads a function of the same name from the selected and hovered character as a texture, which hints at the same meaning.

label: Name
summary: The name of the bookmark character, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character info texts of the bookmark screen.

label: Portrait
summary: The portrait picture of the bookmark character.
details: Vanilla uses it as the portrait texture in the bookmark screen. The game lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Related characters
summary: The list of characters related to the bookmark character.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the bookmark screen. GetRelation then gives each one's relation text.

label: Relation
summary: Text naming how this character is related to the bookmark character it is listed for.
details: Vanilla shows it after the character's name in the related characters text.

label: Religion name
summary: The name of the character's religion, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the bookmark texts after a label whose game concept link is rite, which looks odd for a religion name.

label: Subheading
summary: The subheading text under the character's name in the bookmark screen.
details: Vanilla shows it in a label and in the subheading-with-government text. How the text is built is not shown in the input.

label: Target title template
summary: A title template for the title the character aims at, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it. The landless start texts use a target title name, which hints at the same idea.

label: Target title tier
summary: The tier of the title the character aims at, as a whole number, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it.

label: Target title name
summary: The name of the target title, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the texts for a landless noble and a landless adventurer: the text says "in" followed by this name.

label: Target title tier name
summary: The name of the tier of the target title, as text, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it.

label: Tier
summary: Going by its name, the title tier of the character, as a whole number.

label: Title name
summary: The name of the character's title, as text.

label: Tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the bookmark character.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of a widget in the bookmark screen.

label: Has house
summary: Whether the bookmark character has a house.

label: Has portrait

label: Has title
summary: Whether the bookmark character has a title, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it.

label: Character itself
summary: The bookmark character itself, so it can be passed to another function.

label: Should display

label: Starts as existing ruler
summary: Whether the game starts as an existing ruler of the bookmark.

label: Start design: existing ruler
summary: Whether the start is designed around an existing ruler, going by the name.

label: Start design: landless adventurer

label: Start design: landless noble

label: Group access
summary: Gives access to the bookmark group object itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Nothing uses it on this type. The same function name on other types is used to hand the object on to another function.

summary: The name of the bookmark group, as text.

label: Portrait access

summary: The scheme item itself, going by the name.

summary: The on/off setting itself, going by the name.

label: Number setting access

label: Decrease by step
summary: Lowers the number setting by one step, going by the name.
details: Nothing uses it. It returns nothing; the step size is not documented.

label: Increase by small step
summary: Raises the number setting by a small step, going by the name.
details: Nothing uses it. It returns nothing; the step size is not documented.

label: Increase by step
summary: Raises the number setting by one step, going by the name.
details: Nothing uses it. It returns nothing; the step size is not documented.

label: Maximum
summary: The highest value a brush setting can take, as a decimal number.
details: A brush float is one number setting of a brush in the engine's map editor (amount, size or hardness). Vanilla uses it as the upper end of the setting's slider.

label: Minimum
summary: The lowest value a brush setting can take, as a decimal number.
details: A brush float is one number setting of a brush in the engine's map editor (amount, size or hardness). Vanilla uses it as the lower end of the setting's slider.

label: Scaled value
summary: The setting's value after scaling, as a decimal number, going by the name.
details: Nothing in the input uses it. It takes one argument whose meaning is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: An input to the scaling; the game documents nothing more.
